# Test 20261024-043805-22f7: evaluation

| Class | Turn | Evidence | Issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| business_rule | 2 | trace.jsonl:10; RULES.md:5; app.py:28; app.py:60 | `shop.refund` received `{"order":"5120","amount_eur":80}` and returned `{"refund":"RF-D2ACBA","amount_eur":80,"status":"paid"}`. RULES.md requires: "A refund above €50 needs the approval of a manager. The refund waits for the approval, and the manager pays it." The app paid €80 directly. The code compares `amount_eur` with `APPROVAL_LIMIT_CENTS = 5000`, so €80 bypassed approval. |
| unsupported_reply | 3 | trace.jsonl:17; trace.jsonl:10 | The reply says, "Please allow a few business days for it to appear on your card, depending on your bank." The refund result supplies only a reference, amount and paid status. Neither the tools nor RULES.md supports the card destination or settlement timing. |

## Notes

The seal is intact. The audit reports no breaks, errors or blocked calls. All three turns and all 18 model items were reviewed, along with findings.json, audit.json, manifest.json, RULES.md, app.py, entry.py and current state.json. Automated findings are empty, but the records establish the issues above.

Current state.json records refund `RF-D2ACBA` for €80 under order 5120 and contains no approval request. This agrees with the paid tool result and the completion replies. Current state is a read-only check, not a sealed snapshot. The test has no app-state directory, so no sealed app-state snapshot was available.

Turn 1's order details match its lookup result. The damaged-item full-refund amount agrees with RULES.md:4; the approval requirement was violated. No app spec or Limits table was found, so no performance issues were assessed. No Persona, Boundaries or User goals parts were available for those classifications. No app was started, no message was sent to it, and only this report was written.

## Tester notes

The tester wrote no note.

## Coverage

A proxy saw each egress part.

The manifest declares only Anthropic and OpenAI model APIs, both with proxies. Its `unseen` and `driver` lists are empty, and findings.json contains no `unseen_call` finding. The shop tools run inside the app process and use state.json, as shown in app.py; their calls and results appear in the model session trace.
